title: Finite-pushforward reduction of the tensor comparison
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $S'$ be $K$-schemes and let $g:T\to S'$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism. Put $X'=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $p:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K$, put $k=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $\pi:X_i\to X$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a $k$-module sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Write $M=\pi_*\underline{k}$, with constant sheaf as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $X'_i=X_i\times_X X'$, $Y_i=X'_i\times_{X'}Y$, and write $p_i:X'_i\to X_i$, $\pi':X'_i\to X'$, $\rho:Y_i\to Y$, $h_i:Y_i\to X'_i$, $f_i'=f'\pi'$ and $e_i=e\rho$ for the induced maps. Work in $D^+(-_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and direct and inverse images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Finite exchange, the finite projection formula, and derived direct-image composition give canonical isomorphisms
$$p^{-1}M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\cong\pi'_* (f_i')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F,$$
$$Rh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)\cong\pi'_*Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F.$$
Under these isomorphisms the comparison adjoint to $1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_g$ equals $\pi'_*$ of the untensored comparison $(f_i')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\to Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F$ adjoint to $e_i^{-1}\varepsilon_g$. In particular invertibility of the latter implies invertibility of the former.

proof.text: Promote underived finite exchange to the specified unbounded derived exchange. On a complex, derivedBaseChangeMap_app_fac in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.BaseChange.DerivedUnboundedFac expresses exchange between the exact-derived unit and counit maps as the termwise underived exchange. All three other maps are isomorphisms, because both finite direct images and inverse image are exact. Every derived object is isomorphic to Q of a complex; naturality transports invertibility to it. This uses the factorization API in the module of lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-acyclic-criterion, rather than its more general acyclicity criterion.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward diagram and calculation

proof.text: Compose derived exchange with the canonical inverse-image unit isomorphism. The coefficient ring ULift(F_ell) is additively torsion, since it is finite. Apply the proper torsion projection formula to pi-prime and rho, with the tensor unit as first argument. Tensoring exchange, applying projection and applying the left unitor proves invertibility of each finiteConstantTensorReduction. The target reduction is then a functorial image followed by the inverse conjugate of the square inverse-image isomorphism, so is invertible too.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward diagram and calculation

proof.text: Prove equality of the specified maps by transposing under the composite pi-prime/h_i adjunction. The conjugate counit identity identifies this transpose with the one under the h/rho composite, preceded by the inverse square isomorphism. Naturality of the Hom equivalence gives the two successive transposes. The projection transpose formula identifies each with its tensor comparison followed by the counit, tensoring with the identity, and the left unitor. The derived exchange counit identity identifies rho^*(h^*(a) followed by exchange) followed by the counit with the square isomorphism followed by h_i^*(pi-prime^*(a) followed by the counit). Compatibility of the square isomorphism with tensor comparison (derivedSquareUpperStarIso_hom_tensor), tensor naturality, and inverse-image left-unitor compatibility identify the resulting composites. These are closed source-library APIs in LowerStarProjectionBaseChange and UpperStarMonoidal.Unit. Formal private lemmas establish the calculation for arbitrary bifunctors between categories and comparison natural transformations before specializing. Injectivity of the composite Hom equivalence gives the desired equality.
